title: wt sync fixup --json
description: What `wt sync fixup <rev> --json` prints on stdout: one object, for a fixup committed, one a --dry-run would commit, or a refusal. A refusal exits non-zero; a command line wt cannot read prints no object and exits non-zero. Schema 1: fields may be added and enumerations may gain values; nothing is renamed or removed. See docs/json.md.

schema.description: The major version: a new one only for a change that breaks readers.

schemaVersion.description: The full semantic version of this schema that the output follows.

dryRun.description: Whether --dry-run asked for the look, which writes nothing.

branch.description: The branch the commit goes on; null when the line was not read.

layer.description: The layer branch the commit is in; the line's own branch above the top layer.

target.description: The commit of the line the fixup is for; null when the refusal came before it was found.

sha.description: The commit made; null for a dry run.

subject.description: The fixup! subject asked for, naming the target by its subject, or by an id where that names no one commit.

commit.description: The fixup committed, or that a dry run would commit; null when none is. Set with a refusal only when the branch took the commit although git reported a failure moving it.

files.description: What is staged, which the commit holds; empty when the refusal came before it was read.

status.description: git's letter for the change: A, M, D or T.

refusal.description: Why nothing was committed, or what git reported although the branch took the commit, in the words printed on stderr; null otherwise.
